TRV.rationale: TRV presents a compelling fundamental case anchored by a durable P&C franchise trading at a historically depressed valuation. P/E of 8.6x sits at of 365 range (8.-33x) while ROE sits at  cycle high of 23.8% and operating cash flow exceeds net income ($2.20B vs $1.71B). Q1 2026 results were strong — core income of $1.7B beat consensus by $0.91/share, combined ratio of 88.6%, and $2.2B returned to shareholders including a 14% dividend increase. The franchise is high-quality: second-largest U.S. commercial P&C writer, disciplined underwriting (2025 combined ratio 93.1% vs industry), deep agent distribution, and $1.5B+ annual tech investment. The main caveat is that the annualized EPS range ($26-$33) is extrapolated from non-contiguous quarterly data with a Q4 gap, and cat-loss volatility means any single quarter can swing dramatically (Q1 2025: $1.70 EPS). Revenue growth is minimal at +1% YoY. The P/E compression from 14.6x to 8.6x over 12 months is not driven by deteriorating fundamentals but by earnings normalizing upward while price stayed flat — a genuine dislocation. The Q1 2026 earnings beat and $5B buyback authorization (Jan 2026) provide a near-term rerating path, though the stock has not yet responded. Score of +0.45 reflects strong fundamentals and cheap valuation offset by cat-risk inherent to the business model and the non-contiguous data caveat on the annualized earnings estimate.
